pull.title: fix(admin): save what was chosen, never what the defaults happened to be
pull.body:
## The dashboard was writing settings you never chose

Pressing Save on one field wrote **every** setting in the manifest into
`~/.fcc/.env` as if you had picked it. That is why an install can be carrying
`FALLBACK_BENCH_ENABLED=false` without anyone having set it.

## What was wrong

Two mechanisms, both live until this PR.

**1. Every default was materialised as a user value.**
`target_values_with_updates` (`config/admin/persistence.py:68-98`) started from
`template_values()` — `.env.example` plus `field.default` for every field the
template does not name (`sources.py:63-69`) — overlaid the managed values,
applied the browser's updates, and then ran

```python
for field in FIELDS:
    values.setdefault(field.key, field.default)
```

`render_env_file` (`:256-294`) then wrote all of them as `KEY=value`. So the
first Save of *anything* between v5.58.0 and v5.60.0 wrote
`FALLBACK_BENCH_ENABLED=false`. v5.60.0 changed that default to `true`, but a
managed value outranks the template — so the file kept `false` forever, and
`load_value_state` reported the source as `managed_env`, indistinguishable from
a deliberate choice.

The general failure is bigger than the one setting: **no default could ever
change for an install that had pressed Save once.**

**2. An unset select displayed its first option and then saved it.**
`admin.js:1978-1984` did
`select.value = field.value || field.options[0]?.value || ""`, so a field with
options `("false","true")` and no value showed `false`, while `dataset.original`
stayed `""` (`:1605`). `readFieldValue` returned `"false"` against an original of
`""`, `changedValues()` submitted it, and the next Save persisted it.

**The measured consequence.** With `FALLBACK_BENCH_ENABLED=false`,
`RouteHealthRegistry.enabled` is False, so `FALLBACK_EJECT_AFTER_FAILURES`,
`FALLBACK_EJECT_SECONDS`, `FALLBACK_EJECT_WINDOW`,
`FALLBACK_EJECT_FAILURE_RATE`, `FALLBACK_EJECT_MIN_SAMPLES` and
`FALLBACK_BEHAVIOR=rate_based` are **all inert** — a model that fails half its
requests is retried at chain position 0 on every single request.

## What to expect now

The managed file records choices, never defaults.

| Situation | Managed file | Source | Settings uses |
|---|---|---|---|
| never touched | `# KEY= (default: true)` | `template` / `default` | the code default |
| you set it | `KEY=value` | `managed_env` | your value |
| you set it *to* the default | `KEY=value`, kept | `managed_env` | your value (an explicit choice survives a later default change) |
| you clear it, repo `.env` silent | line removed | `template` / `default` | the code default |
| you clear it, repo `.env` sets it | `KEY=` where the type accepts a blank | `managed_env` | the default, repo value masked |
| the manifest does not own the key | preserved verbatim | — | — |

Where a blank is *not* accepted (a plain `bool` or `int` with no blank
validator) the line is dropped and the save returns a warning naming the key,
shown in the dashboard.

In the UI:

- Every field prints its default underneath it.
- A value that came from the dashboard is badged **set here**, and gets a
  **Use default** button that removes the line.
- Selects have an explicit `Default (…)` option, so an unset field loads clean
  and the form reads "No changes".
- Booleans are three-state selects (`Default (On)` / `On` / `Off`) instead of
  checkboxes — a checkbox has two positions and a setting has three states.

## Action required

**If you never set `FALLBACK_BENCH_ENABLED` yourself, check the Limits page** —
a `false` written by an older dashboard disables chain benching and makes every
Eject setting below it inert. Press **Use default**.

## Known and deliberate

- **Existing managed files are not rewritten.** A value on disk is effective
  configuration; silently changing it would be a worse bug than the one being
  fixed. The fix is surfaced instead — source badge, printed default, one-click
  Use default — and named here.
- The Limits page redesign is PR E. This PR is correctness only.
- Eighteen manifest defaults legitimately differ from the bare code default
  (provider base URLs that name the endpoint an empty default resolves to, and
  fields showing the shipped `.env.example` recommendation). Each is now listed
  with its reason in a contract test that fails if a listed field starts
  matching, so the list cannot rot.

## Verification

Windows, Python 3.14.0:

```
uv run ruff format --check   981 files already formatted
uv run ruff check            All checks passed!
uv run ty check              All checks passed!      (repo-wide)
scripts/ci.ps1 -Only suppressions                    passed
uv run pytest -q --tb=line   15 failed, 6174 passed, 38 skipped in 106.50s
```

The jsdom suite **ran locally** (node v24.6.0, `jsdom` resolved from
`tests/api`): `tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py` 35 passed, including the
three new cases — an unset select loads clean showing `Default (true)`,
"Use default" submits the empty value and marks the form dirty, and boolean
fields render three states.

New tests: `test_a_save_writes_only_what_was_set`,
`test_dotenv_sees_only_set_keys_in_the_rendered_file`,
`test_an_unset_field_follows_a_changed_default`, both blanking branches with
the warning, `test_a_value_equal_to_the_default_is_still_recorded`,
`test_every_manifest_default_matches_the_settings_default`,
`test_apply_with_an_unrelated_field_does_not_write_other_defaults`, and a
static guard asserting `admin.js` no longer contains `field.options[0]?.value`.

### Baseline

The local suite has **15 pre-existing failures that also fail on unmodified
`main`** — 8 websearch / web-server-tool tests that read the real `~/.fcc/.env`,
6 PowerShell installer tests, and
`tests/runtime/test_provider_manager.py::test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`.
GitHub runners have no `~/.fcc`, so they pass there. Nothing to chase.

## Residual risks

1. **Existing installs keep their materialised defaults** until someone presses
   Use default. This PR stops new ones being written; it does not migrate the
   ones already on disk.
2. **A field whose Settings type rejects `""` cannot be blanked while the repo
   `.env` sets it.** The save drops the line and returns a warning saying to
   remove it there; it does not fail silently, but it also cannot do what was
   asked.
3. **Three-state booleans change the look of every boolean field** on the
   settings pages, including the Token Optimizer's proxied switch (which now
   reads the effective value rather than a checkbox's `checked`).
4. **The admin's prediction of Settings changed where a default was previously
   materialised.** Concretely, an install with no `VOICE_NOTE_ENABLED` line now
   reports the Hugging Face key as the live voice credential and asks for a
   restart when it changes. This matches what the running server already did;
   it is the admin that was wrong before.

commit.message:
fix(admin): save what was chosen, never what the defaults happened to be

A user's managed env carried `FALLBACK_BENCH_ENABLED=false`, which they never
set. `RouteHealthRegistry.enabled` was therefore False, so
FALLBACK_EJECT_AFTER_FAILURES, FALLBACK_EJECT_SECONDS, FALLBACK_EJECT_WINDOW,
FALLBACK_EJECT_FAILURE_RATE, FALLBACK_EJECT_MIN_SAMPLES and
FALLBACK_BEHAVIOR=rate_based were all inert on that install, and a flapping
model was retried at chain position 0 on every request.

Two mechanisms wrote that line, both live until now.

The first: the managed file materialised every manifest default as if the user
had chosen it. `target_values_with_updates` (config/admin/persistence.py:68-98)
started from `template_values()` -- `.env.example` plus `field.default` for
every field the template does not name (sources.py:63-69) -- overlaid the
managed values, applied the browser's updates, then ran
`for field in FIELDS: values.setdefault(field.key, field.default)` (:96-97).
`render_env_file` (:256-294) wrote every one of them as `KEY=value`. So the
first Save of *anything* between v5.58.0 and v5.60.0 wrote
`FALLBACK_BENCH_ENABLED=false`; v5.60.0 changed the default to `true`, but a
managed value outranks the template, so the file kept `false` forever. The
general failure is worse than the one setting: **no default could ever change
for an install that had pressed Save once**, and `load_value_state`
(values.py:67-91) then reported the source as `managed_env`, indistinguishable
from a deliberate choice.

The second: an unset select rendered as its first option and then counted as an
edit. `admin.js:1978-1984` did
`select.value = field.value || field.options[0]?.value || ""`, so a field with
options ("false","true") and no value displayed `false`, while
`buildFieldControl` set `dataset.original = field.value || ""` (:1605).
`readFieldValue` returned "false" against an original of "", `changedValues()`
submitted it, and the next Save persisted it.

The contract now: a field nobody set is written as a commented placeholder
naming its default (`# FALLBACK_BENCH_ENABLED= (default: true)`) and dotenv
sees only the set keys, so the code default applies and a later release can
still change it. A field the user set is written as `KEY=value` and reported as
`managed_env` -- including when the value equals the default, because an
explicit choice has to survive a change of that default. Clearing a field
removes its line, so the layer underneath shows through again; the one
exception is a key the repo `.env` also sets, where only an explicit `KEY=`
outranks it, and that is written only where the Settings type accepts a blank.
Where it does not -- a plain bool or int with no blank validator -- the line is
dropped and the save returns a warning naming the key. Unmanaged keys are still
preserved verbatim.

Non-obvious choices:

* `settings_from_values` now omits absent keys from the kwargs instead of
  passing "". With defaults no longer materialised, "" would reach every bool
  and int that has no blank validator; omitting the key gives the Settings
  default, which is exactly what the server does when it loads the file.
  This makes the admin's prediction match the runtime: an install with no
  VOICE_NOTE_ENABLED line now correctly reports the Hugging Face key as the
  live voice credential.
* The blank-accepting set is `BLANK_MEANS_UNSET_FIELDS`, extracted from the
  inline validator list in config/settings.py so the admin layer and the
  Settings model read one list rather than two that can drift.
* Booleans render as three-state selects, not checkboxes: a checkbox has two
  positions and a setting has three states. The optimizer's proxied switch and
  segmented controls read `effectiveControlValue()` so an unset control still
  draws its default.
* Every field prints its default underneath, `managed_env` is labelled "set
  here" instead of blank, and a field that was set gets a "Use default" button
  that submits the empty value. Secrets and model chains are excluded: both
  already have their own editor and a second way to clear them would
  contradict it.
* `test_every_manifest_default_matches_the_settings_default` generalises the
  limits-only contract to every field with a `settings_attr`. Eighteen fields
  legitimately differ -- provider base URLs that name the endpoint the empty
  code default resolves to, and fields whose manifest shows the shipped
  `.env.example` recommendation -- and each is listed with its reason; the test
  fails if a listed field starts matching, so the list cannot rot.

Verification (Windows, Python 3.14.0):

    uv run ruff format --check   981 files already formatted
    uv run ruff check            All checks passed!
    uv run ty check              All checks passed! (repo-wide)
    scripts/ci.ps1 -Only suppressions   passed
    uv run pytest -q --tb=line   15 failed, 6174 passed, 38 skipped

The 15 are the standing local baseline that also fails on unmodified `main`:
8 websearch/web-server-tool tests that read the real ~/.fcc/.env, 6 PowerShell
installer tests, and
tests/runtime/test_provider_manager.py::test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache.
The jsdom suite ran locally (node v24.6.0, jsdom resolved): 35 passed,
including the three new unset/default/three-state cases.

Deliberately not done: existing managed files are not rewritten. A value on
disk is effective configuration and silently changing it would be a worse bug
than the one being fixed; the release notes name FALLBACK_BENCH_ENABLED and
point at the Use default button instead. The Limits page redesign is PR E.
